newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes down at 2,400-2,500 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes down at 2,400-2,500 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 2,400-2,500 per dollar, down from midday's 2,200-2,300 and the morning's 2,120-2,180, on a rise in foreign currency demand to cover short positions, dealers said.
"Large final clients started bidding for dollars more actively in the afternoon, which led to a lev fall by some 400 on the day," one dealer said.
The dollar short-covering began on Thursday afternoon and kept pressure on the lev, which revived expectations of further lev drops, traders said.
As a result, traders expected dollar supply to be low next week, traders said.

"This week's lev rise was largely psychological. It was not supported by positive changes in economic factors, and it is is natural for the market to aim at higher rates for the dollar especially when demand rises," another dealer said.

The lev had risen to 2,000-2,080 on Thursday from around 2,800 on Monday on a rise in dollar supply after the central bank governor said the lev was undervalued and the finance minister raised the possibility of a lev rise to 2,000. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 9818569
